Alex (eng-runtime): quick heads up — after rolling runtime v3.4.1 (kernel-profile + quant tweak) to canary we’re seeing a regression in prefix/priming hit-rate on medium/long prompts (~50-300 tokens).
Mira (perf): how big is the delta? numbers?
Alex (eng-runtime): overall hit-rate down ~18% on g4dn pools; specific workload (customer A) warmup now takes ~6 requests instead of ~2. p50 generation latency unaffected, p95+p99 +30-60ms.
Sam (infra): did routing or batching configs change with the build? the scheduler tweak landed yesterday.
Alex (eng-runtime): not intentionally — build included a kernel affinity change and the quant profile switched to 4-bit-e4 for a few matrix paths. also we flipped the batching heuristic that favors slightly larger per-GPU batches.
Jen (eng-runtime): can you paste a short profiler capture and an example cache key diff?
Alex (eng-runtime): yes — profiler snippet from a failed warmup request:
```
[profiler] timeline: dispatch -> kernel_select (fused_attn_v2) -> run_kernel (quant_e4_path) -> kv_lookup (miss) -> generate chunks
kernel_select: chose fused_attn_v2 (new affinity) vs fused_attn_legacy previously
kv_lookup: key shard mismatch: key_hash=0x7f3a vs expected 0x3b1d for same prompt across runs
```
Mira (perf): that hash mismatch smells like key canonicalization or padding differences. did tokenizer behavior change with the quantized kernel?
Alex (eng-runtime): tokenizer config unchanged. but the kernel affinity reorders padding/trail bytes for alignment — observed different trailing-zero normalization in the code path, which affects key derivation (we prepend kernel buildid and padlen).
Sam (infra): the batching heuristic change might also change request arrival order and batching boundaries, which affects cache key construction if we include timestamped session ids. are we including any non-deterministic metadata in keys?
Jen (eng-runtime): keys are: sha256(buildid || model_name || prompt_norm || padlen || session_hint). session_hint should be stable, but padlen came from kernel alignment math.
Mira (perf): run a quick A/B: same prompt -> run old runtime image vs new on same machine and compare keys and KV hit rate. can we repro locally?
Alex (eng-runtime): repro on local gpu-direct. Old image (v3.4.0) warmup hit sequence: HIT, HIT, HIT. New image (v3.4.1): MISS, MISS, HIT. I saved the key list (short):
```
old keys: [a1b2..., a1b2..., a1b2...]
new keys: [a1b2..., b7c9..., a1b2...]
```
Mira (perf): looks like padlen produced b7c9 variant on second request. patch idea: remove padlen from key derivation and rely on normalized prompt_norm and buildid only — safer but may increase false hits if alignment affects output.
Sam (infra): another angle: ensure kernel-select doesn't embed runtime-specific transient metadata into buildid. maybe we should canonicalize buildid to model/arch-only.
Jen (eng-runtime): agreed. two-pronged mitigation: 1) normalize key derivation (drop padlen + canonicalize buildid), 2) rollback kernel-affinity tweak on canary until we verify.
Alex (eng-runtime): I ran a quick experiment removing padlen from key derivation: hit-rate returned to baseline in the canary tests, p95 latency unchanged. still need to check safety across different sequence lengths.
Mira (perf): please run a short sweep: 50 prompts across lengths [10,50,150,300] with randomized seeds — compare hit-rate, p95/p99, and token throughput. put results in the perf dashboard.
Alex (eng-runtime): starting now.
ci-bot: perf-suite/kv-warmup-sweep started — run id: perf-1745010500.
Sam (infra): one more caution: if we drop padlen we may get accidental collisions for prompts with different alignment that would have diverged previously; need to run a collision analysis.
Jen (eng-runtime): collision analysis plan: sample 10k prompts from traffic bucket, compute keys with old and new derivation, and measure collision delta and any corresponding generation divergence in a downstream eval harness.
Mira (perf): timeline? if we can get the sweep + collision analysis done in 2-3 hours we can make a canary decision today.
Alex (eng-runtime): I’ll coordinate. initial perf-sweep shows hit-rate back to +1% of baseline within 15 mins. pushing collision-job now.
ci-bot: perf-job perf-1745010500 finished: hit_rate_delta=+1.3%, p95_delta=+0.0ms, p99_delta=+45ms (noise).
Mira (perf): p99 jitter likely noise — run a second run. also add test on quant_e4_path with longer context 1024 tokens.
Alex (eng-runtime): second run queued. if both look good we’ll submit key-normalization PR and cut a hotfix with kernel-affinity disabled on canary.
Jen (eng-runtime): create PR with clear migration notes: mention previous key scheme and reason for change so on-disk caches remain consistent. we should also add a compatibility flag to opt-in older behavior for debugging.
Sam (infra): after hotfix, monitor global warmup hit-rate + error rates for 24h on canary. set alert if warmup latency > baseline + 100ms or hit-rate drop > 5%.
Mira (perf): logging checklist: capture (a) example key diffs, (b) sample request traces with kernel_select decisions, (c) profiling timestamps for kv_lookup.
Alex (eng-runtime): will attach logs to the PR. thanks all, will update thread with the PR link and roll plan.
Jen (eng-runtime): thanks — appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
